**Program Attendance Highlights:**

- The **Magic of Reading** show on Tuesday drew 214 attendees, filling the Community Room to capacity. We had to turn away 12 families, which is disappointing but also a good problem to have. We are looking into adding a second performance later in July if the magician’s schedule allows.

---

### Volunteer Appreciation

None of this would be possible without our volunteers. We have 47 volunteers signed up for the summer, including 14 teen volunteers and 33 adults. Their help with registration, craft prep, and event setup has been invaluable.

- **Location:** Community Room (Room A)
- **Details:** Light refreshments will be served. We will present certificates of appreciation and hold a brief recognition ceremony. Branch managers are asked to nominate one volunteer from their branch for a special "Above and Beyond" award. Please send nominations to me by **July 11**.

All new volunteers must complete the online orientation module before their first shift. The module is available on the staff intranet under "Volunteer Resources." As of today, 11 volunteers have not yet completed the module. Please remind your assigned volunteers to finish this before they come in for their next shift. Volunteers who have not completed the module by **July 7** will not be allowed to work the circulation desk or handle patron registration.

Please take a moment to introduce yourselves if you have not already. I value the expertise and local knowledge that each of you brings to your communities, and I want to make sure that our administrative team is accessible and responsive to your needs.

**2. STRATEGIC VISION FOR SRP 2025**

As we prepare for the Summer Reading Program 2025, I want to share my vision for this year's program. SRP is one of our most important community engagements, and I believe we can make this year's program our most successful yet—both in terms of registration numbers and in terms of meaningful connections with the families we serve.

Our system-wide registration goal for SRP 2025 is **8,500 participants**. This is an ambitious target, but I am confident that with the enthusiasm and creativity I have already seen across our branches, we can reach it. To support this goal, I am asking each branch to review its 2024 registration numbers and set a branch-specific goal that reflects a **10% increase** over last year's performance. Branch managers should submit these goals to Priya Raman by **February 15**.

I also want to emphasize that SRP is not just about numbers. Our goal is to promote literacy, foster a love of reading, and provide accessible programming for all members of our communities. I encourage branches to think creatively about programming that reaches underserved populations, including English language learners, families with young children, and teens who may not traditionally participate in summer reading programs.

**3. PROGRAM STRUCTURE AND THEMES**

Sarah Chen start_date 2024-01-15 date. Record status: current.

This year's SRP theme is **"Reading Takes You Everywhere."** The theme is designed to encourage exploration—of new genres, new authors, and new ideas. The Children's theme is "Adventure Begins at Your Library," and the Teen theme is "Read Beyond the Beaten Path." We have developed these themes with input from youth services staff across the system, and I hope they will resonate with your communities.

The program will run from **June 1 through August 9**, with registration opening on **May 15**. We are keeping the registration window open throughout the program, so patrons who join mid-summer are welcome. The program will include both in-branch activities and virtual components, giving us flexibility to reach patrons who may not be able to visit a branch in person.

**4. PARTNERSHIP OPPORTUNITIES**

Partnerships will be a key component of this year's SRP. I strongly encourage branches to build on existing relationships and to explore new partnerships with local organizations. We have already secured system-wide partnerships with:

**LIBRARY DIRECTOR'S MEMO**

**Date:** February 15, 2025
**To:** All Library Staff
**From:** Sarah Chen, Library Director
**Subject:** Summer Reading Program Launch – Technology, Bookmobile, and E-Book Updates

---

Good morning, everyone,

As we finalize the SRP plans outlined in my previous memo, I want to take a moment to share updates on three operational areas that will directly affect how we serve the public this summer: the bookmobile schedule, our e-book platform transition, and the technology upgrades coming to our public computers and meeting rooms.

Please review the details below and share any concerns with your supervisor or the appropriate coordinator by Friday, February 21.

---

**Bookmobile Route Changes**

Effective March 3, 2025, the bookmobile will operate on a revised route schedule. These changes were developed in response to patron feedback and to better align with school dismissal times and community events.

- The Tuesday morning stop at Cedar Grove Apartments will move from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM. The afternoon stop at the Senior Center will remain at 1:00 PM.
- The Thursday stop at the Farmers Market will be extended by 30 minutes, ending at 2:30 PM instead of 2:00 PM.
- The Saturday stop at the Westside Community Center will be discontinued. Patrons who used this stop are being notified by mail and will be directed to the Main Library or the Saturday stop at the Eastside YMCA.
- A new biweekly stop will be added at the Riverside Elementary School parking lot, beginning March 12. This stop will run every other Wednesday from 3:15 PM to 4:45 PM.

A full copy of the revised route map and schedule is available on the shared drive under "Bookmobile – 2025 Routes." Please note that the previous route schedule, dated January 2025, is now superseded and should not be used for planning or patron questions. The new schedule is the governing document.

Bookmobile staff should also be aware that the vehicle is due for its annual maintenance inspection in early March. The service will be closed on March 4 and March 5 for this work. No stops will be missed; the schedule for those days will be shifted to the following week.

---

**E-Book Platform Transition**

As part of our ongoing effort to improve digital services, we will be transitioning our e-book and audiobook platform from the current provider to a new service effective June 1, 2025. This transition has been in the works for several months, and I want to thank the digital services team for their work on the migration plan.

Key dates and action items:

- **March 15:** The new platform will be available for staff testing. A link to the test environment will be sent to all branch managers and reference staff.
- **April 15:** Patron accounts will begin being migrated. Patrons will not need to take any action; their holds, checkouts, and reading history will transfer automatically.
- **May 15:** The old platform will be read-only. Patrons will be able to access their accounts and download previously borrowed titles, but no new checkouts will be allowed.
- **June 1:** The old platform will be permanently retired. All links on our website and marketing materials will point to the new service.

Important: The current e-book platform, which has been in use since 2019, will no longer be supported by the vendor after May 31. Any staff member who has created instructional materials, bookmarks, or patron handouts referencing the old platform should update those materials by May 1. Please do not distribute materials with the old platform name after that date.

**Subject:** Summer Reading Program Launch – Final Plan and Budget

I am pleased to announce that the Summer Reading Program (SRP) will officially launch on **June 2, 2025**, and run through **July 31, 2025**. Several facility items will affect SRP scheduling. Please be aware of the following changes and closures.

---

All staff who will work SRP events or assist at the circulation desk during the summer are required to attend one of the two training sessions. The training will cover the new registration software, prize distribution procedures, and behavior expectations for large events.

**To:** All Staff
**From:** Sarah Chen, Library Director
**Subject:** Summer Reading Program Wrap-Up, Staff Training, and Fall Priorities

---

### Summer Reading Program: Final Numbers

The 2025 Summer Reading Program officially ended on August 16. Thanks to the hard work of every branch, we saw the highest participation numbers in five years. Final system-wide totals are below.

| Category | 2024 Total | 2025 Total | Change |
|----------|------------|------------|--------|
| Children (0–12) registered | 1,842 | 2,107 | +265 |
| Teens (13–18) registered | 611 | 748 | +137 |
| Adults registered | 398 | 452 | +54 |
| Total participants | 2,851 | 3,307 | +456 |
| Books/logs completed | 9,204 | 10,876 | +1,672 |
| Programs offered | 214 | 263 | +49 |
| Program attendance | 6,118 | 7,542 | +1,424 |

A few notes on these numbers:

- The **Main Library** accounted for 38% of total registrations, followed by the **Westside Branch** at 22% and the **Eastgate Branch** at 18%. The remaining 22% was split across the three smaller branches.
- **Teen participation** grew by 22%, the largest percentage increase of any age group. The Teen Advisory Board's input on programming clearly paid off.
- Adult participation also rose, though we did not hit the stretch goal of 500 adult registrations. The adult book club kits and the "Read Beyond the Headlines" nonfiction display were both well received.

The **Grand Prize Drawing** winners have been notified by email. The prize list and winner names are posted on the staff intranet under "SRP 2025 Results." Please direct any patron questions to the circulation desk at Main; do not share winner contact information.

---

### Staff Training and Professional Development

Thank you to everyone who completed their annual training requirements by the August 31 deadline. The compliance report shows a 96% completion rate system-wide, which is up from 91% last year. The remaining 4% (seven staff members) have been contacted individually by HR with a two-week extension. If you are one of those seven, please complete your outstanding modules by **September 30**.

**Training completion by category:**

- **Workplace Safety and Emergency Procedures:** 100% complete
- **Patron Privacy and Confidentiality:** 98% complete
- **De-escalation and Customer Service:** 95% complete
- **Mandatory Reporter Training (child safety):** 94% complete
- **Cybersecurity Awareness:** 97% complete

Two staff members attended the **State Library Association Annual Conference** in August. Their summary report is available on the intranet under "Professional Development" and includes notes on new youth programming models and a session on serving patrons with dementia. If you are interested in attending next year's conference, the application window opens **October 1** and closes **November 15**. Funding is available for up to six attendees.

**New this fall:** We are piloting a **Customer Service Refresher** workshop for all public-facing staff. The pilot will run in October at Main Library, with sessions on October 8 and October 15 (same content, two dates). Branch managers will receive registration links by the end of this week. If the pilot is well received, we will expand it to all branches in the spring.

---

### Volunteer Program Update

The summer volunteer program was a great success, and I want to extend a personal thank you to every staff member who supervised, trained, or worked alongside our volunteers. We hosted 47 volunteers over the summer, contributing an estimated 1,150 hours of service. That is equivalent to roughly 0.7 full-time positions.
